sources_quoted.conclusion: In this cache the first {{rd}} argument is the MELEE value and the second is the RANGED value, keyed off the item HOLDER, not the target.

sources_quoted.note: The document contains no Bloodsong / Expose Weakness / support-amplifier entry, so it neither supports nor contradicts this leaf. Damage amplifiers of this form are ordinary multiplicative pre-mitigation factors under §2.1's `post = raw · m(R)` decomposition.

independent_computation.step_1_effect: Bloodsong's Spellblade proc, when the empowered basic attack hits an enemy CHAMPION, applies 'Expose Weakness' for 4 s (1.5 s cooldown starting on the empowered attack).
independent_computation.step_2_magnitude: Expose Weakness makes the debuffed target take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from ALL sources — 8% if the Bloodsong holder is melee, 5% if the holder is ranged (S1 + S2).
independent_computation.step_3_form: "X% increased damage taken" is a multiplicative amplifier on the damage instance, i.e. multiplier = 1 + X/100.
independent_computation.result: 1.08 for a melee Bloodsong holder; 1.05 for a ranged holder. The baseline's 1.08 is exactly the sourced melee branch, and the attribution string 'Bloodsong — Expose Weakness' names the correct effect.
independent_computation.old_value_assessment: The previous state (leaf absent) asserts no amplifier at all, which contradicts S1 outright for any roster in which the Bloodsong holder lands a Spellblade-empowered attack on an enemy champion. 'absent' cannot be the correct value for a scenario deliberately named after Bloodsong; the only sourced values are 1.08 and 1.05.

caveat.residual_uncertainty: The melee/ranged branch is selected by the Bloodsong HOLDER's attack type. The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' lives outside the permitted evidence tree (tests/ and scripts/), so this oracle could not read the holder's champion and cannot discriminate 1.08 from 1.05 by direct inspection of the roster.
caveat.why_new_value_correct_was_still_returned: 1.08 reproduces a sourced value of the correct effect with the correct multiplicative form and the correct attribution, whereas the old state (absent) reproduces no sourced value at all. Nothing in the permitted tree indicates a ranged holder; the scenario pairs Bloodsong with Black Cleaver, a melee-flavoured physical-damage build. The verdict is therefore new_value_correct, conditional on the holder being melee.
caveat.falsifier: If the Bloodsong carrier in 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' has attackRange > 300 (ranged) per data/champions.json, this leaf must be 1.05, not 1.08, and the verdict flips to both_wrong. That single check is the whole remaining risk and can be settled by whoever can read the scenario roster.
